scenes.headline: How do headphones erase sound?
scenes.narration: Put on noise-cancelling headphones and a plane engine just fades away. It feels like magic, but it is physics.

scenes.headline: Microphones listen first
scenes.narration: Tiny microphones on the outside of each ear cup constantly listen to the noise around you.

scenes.headline: Then they flip the wave
scenes.narration: A chip builds a mirror image of that sound, a wave that is exactly upside down, and plays it through the speaker.

scenes.headline: Two waves cancel out
scenes.narration: When a wave meets its mirror image, they add up to almost nothing. Engineers call this destructive interference.

stat.label: what two mirror waves add up to

scenes.headline: Where it works best
scenes.narration: It is best at steady, low sounds. Sudden or high sounds are harder to predict, so padding still does some of the work.

scenes.headline: Next time, listen closely
scenes.narration: Next time you fly, notice how the engine hum disappears. That silence is a wave cancelling itself.
